body:
alex: seeing a huge UDP pulse hitting embeddings-ops (ingress) from tons of spoofed sources, pattern looks NTP-like. qps spiked to ~600k. tagging @emily_sre @jamal @maria_sec
security-bot: ALERT: unusual_udp_amplification pattern detected for service=embeddings-ops, score=0.94, rule=net-amp-heuristic-v3
emily_sre: on it. initial PCAPs show NTP monlist-style payloads + short TTLs. multiple origin ASNs, likely reflection/amplification abuse.
jamal: I can push quick mitigations at edge. proposing: 1) temporary per-ASN nullroute for top offenders 2) tighten per-src rate-limit on /v1/embeddings 3) WAF rule to drop known NTP reflection signatures
jamal: pushing nullroute now for ASN 39712 and ASN 29876. doing upstream-blackhole via edge-provider API
jamal: command used:
```
# provider api
POST /v1/peering/blackholes
{"prefix":"198.51.100.0/24","reason":"ntp-amplifier-quick-blackhole"}
```
emily_sre: added a WAF quick-rule (temp) to drop UDP packets larger than 200 bytes to port 123 and to block requests with monlist patterns. rule id waf-ntp-temp-17645
maria_sec: approved emergency WAF change in #sec-approvals. Quick question: who can roll this back? we need RBAC trace and audit for the change.
ops-bot: Audit event recorded: actor=jamal, action=waf.rule.create, rule_id=waf-ntp-temp-17645, ts=1764501258
maria_sec: good. make sure audit logs are forwarded to SIEM and retained. also flag for post-incident RBAC review — tighten who can make ad-hoc WAF edits.
emily_sre: traffic is down ~85% after blackhole + WAF rule, embeddings latency back to normal for most customers. still seeing low-volume probes.
alex: customer-impact? any client complaints?
nina_pm: Ops on-call reported 2 support tickets from customers with heavy embed usage complaining about timeouts between 09:12-09:24 UTC. we'll send a status update after triage.
jamal: note — we also temporarily disabled cross-region fallback for embeddings to avoid routing loops. recording in changelog.
maria_sec: follow-ups: 1) create a postmortem 2) add a dedicated detection rule in SIEM for NTP-like amplification (not just net heuristics) 3) RBAC: scope WAF edit to sec-admins + network-ops only 4) verify audit retention policy (30 days -> 90 days?) 5) check KMS access logs for any key activity (no indication yet but include in triage)
emily_sre: on vuln triage: this looks like external abuse, no application vuln found. will confirm there is no exploit path in our embedding endpoint.
alex: agree — not an app vuln. still add a note to the security board to review any exposed UDP services and customer onboarding that might enable reflection targets.
jamal: created infra ticket INF-4829 for permanent mitigations: edge-rate-limits, per-prefix ACLs, and BGP shunt playbook. assigned to jamal.
maria_sec: created sec ticket SEC-1721 for RBAC audit & audit-log retention. assigning to me.
ops-bot: created support ticket SUP-9152 with affected customer list and time window.
nina_pm: I'll draft a short customer comms template for impacted customers and post in #customer-success for review.
emily_sre: proposed post-incident action items also include automated rollback safeties for quick WAF rules and a canary for embeddings to detect collateral drops.
maria_sec: action owner matrix: jamal (mitigations + permanent infra), emily_sre (forensics + SIEM rule), maria_sec (RBAC & audits), nina_pm (customer comms).
alex: thanks team. schedule a 30-min postmortem tomorrow 14:00 UTC. please attach PCAPs, edge metrics, and audit entries to the PM. :thumbsup:
security-bot: NOTE: recommend KMS key-check: verify that no TLS/private key rotations were triggered during the incident; if any API keys show anomalous usage, rotate via KMS and log the operation.
maria_sec: acknowledged. will add KMS verification to SEC-1721.
ops-bot: closing thread for now, will reopen if traffic resurges.
